Posterior draws of one smooth term

Source: R/posterior_smooths.mvgam.R
posterior_smooths.mvgam.Rd

Evaluates one smooth at the rows of newdata for each posterior draw, in the shape brms::posterior_smooths() returns. The smooth can be any s() or t2() term of the observation formula, a distributional or non-linear parameter's formula, or the trend formula, by factors included.

Usage

# S3 method for mvgam
posterior_smooths(
  object,
  smooth,
  newdata = NULL,
  resp = NULL,
  dpar = NULL,
  nlpar = NULL,
  ndraws = NULL,
  draw_ids = NULL,
  ...
)

Arguments

object

A fitted mvgam object.

smooth

The smooth term as the formula writes it, such as "s(x)", "s(z, by = group)" or "t2(x, y)". Spacing is ignored. smooths.mvgam() lists the terms.

newdata

A data.frame holding the smooth's own variables, or NULL for the training data.

resp

The response the smooth belongs to, required on a model with several.

dpar, nlpar

The distributional or non-linear parameter the smooth belongs to. Name at most one. With both NULL the smooth belongs to the mean.

ndraws, draw_ids

The number of posterior draws, or their indices. Give at most one. NULL for both uses every draw.

...

Unused. Anything passed here is refused.

Value

A numeric matrix with one row per draw and one column per row of newdata: the smooth's contribution to the linear predictor.

Details

The smooth's contribution is its unpenalised basis times its fixed coefficients plus each penalised basis times its random coefficients, per draw. The bases come from brms::standata() evaluated on newdata. The coefficients come from the draws. brms::posterior_smooths() adds a predictor's offsets to each of its smooths. This method leaves them out.

A term written in both the observation and the trend formula is taken from the observation formula.

See also

conditional_smooths.mvgam() summarises every smooth. smooths.mvgam() lists the terms.

Other predictions: conditional_effects.mvgam(), conditional_smooths.mvgam(), fitted.mvgam(), hindcast.mvgam(), posterior_epred.mvgam(), posterior_linpred.mvgam(), posterior_predict.mvgam(), predict.mvgam(), predictive_error.mvgam(), predictive_interval.mvgam()

Author

Nicholas J Clark

Examples

# \dontrun{
set.seed(13)
simdat <- sim_mvgam(family = poisson(), n_series = 1L,
                     n_timepoints = 120L, trend_model = AR())
mod <- mvgam(y ~ s(x), trend_formula = ~ AR(p = 1),
              data    = simdat$data_train,
              family  = poisson(),
              chains  = 2, silent = 2)
#> Warning: 9 of 2000 (0.0%) transitions ended with a divergence.
#> See https://mc-stan.org/misc/warnings for details.

# Twenty draws of s(x) over a grid of x
grid <- data.frame(x = seq(-2, 2, length.out = 50))
sm <- posterior_smooths(mod, smooth = "s(x)", newdata = grid)
matplot(grid$x, t(sm[1:20, ]), type = "l", lty = 1, col = "grey60",
        xlab = "x", ylab = "s(x)")


# Next, conditional_smooths(mod) summarises every smooth in one call
# }
